additionalCoursework:
Two (2) additional sciences are required.  These two courses may include, but are not limited to: Genetics, Microbiology, Comparative Anatomy, Human Anatomy, Biomedical Engineering, Neuroscience, Physics, Virology, Immunology, Medical Botany, Pharmacology, etc.

Also, six (6) credit hours of Humanities courses are required.  The student should know the importance of the role of interdisciplinary topics that ultimately contribute to patient care. These topics are typically fulfilled from general education course requirements in undergraduate studies. These topics are typically fulfilled from coursework in, but not limited to: Art, Music, Theater, Speech and Communication, Foreign Language, Philosophy, Religion, Gender and Women Studies, Ethics, Literature.

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: The Burnett School of Medicine at TCU is committed to embracing and supporting all students.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: Participation in Student Leadership, Student Senate and student organizations, interest groups and Standing Committees is an integral aspect to medical school education. With careful consideration of interests, time availability, and a focus on academics, co-curricular activities provide practical, life skills that will assist you in your medical careers, a way to feel connected to the Burnett School of Medicine, and the means to meet and to connect with your classmates, faculty and staff. Students who participate in leadership positions will: advocate for and serve student needs; create and facilitate innovative student programs and services that promote student success, wellness, and professionalism; participate in continuous improvement processes; and promote, develop, and foster vertical relationships between students from all classes.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: The Burnett School of Medicine at TCU is located in Fort Worth, Texas - the 11th largest city in the United States and a top destination in Texas, welcoming more than 11.5 million visitors annually. Founded in 1873, TCU is a world-class, values-centered private university based in Fort Worth, Texas. The University comprises eight schools and colleges offering 113 areas of undergraduate study, 58 master’s level programs and 30 areas of doctoral study.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Various on and off-campus housing options are available within the vicinity of our campus community.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: The Burnett School of Medicine at TCU is committed to embracing and supporting all students.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: The Burnett School of Medicine at TCU does have support systems and resources in place for applicants and learners with disabilities.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: In an effort to prioritize the holistic development and wellbeing of our medical students, we have a comprehensive initiative that integrates curricular and co-curricular components. The curricular aspect includes dedicated course sessions throughout the four years designed to enhance self-awareness, emotional intelligence, empathy and compassion, personal and professional identity, and servant leadership. Simultaneously, the co-curricular facet of the initiative involves an annual calendar of extracurricular activities aimed at enhancing mental, emotional, relational, and physical health. Our school also provides a student coaching program which focuses on accountability, professionalism and professional identity formation. Additionally, we have a strong system of support networks and social engagement that promotes a sense of community, collaboration, and belonging among students.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: The Burnett School of Medicine at TCU takes a progressive approach to medical education that shapes our Empathetic Scholars® who are both adept at caring for patients and able to meet the health care challenges of tomorrow. Student success and thus, how they care for their patients, is at the heart of the school’s design and has been incorporated in everything from the creation of significant learning experiences and educational spaces to highly individualized team-based framework for ongoing student coaching and support.  The school aims to optimize each student’s experience and performance by using proven strategies in self-directed learning, harnessing new technologies and incorporating longitudinal clinical learning opportunities.  Patient care begins at the time students enter the program and integrates across the curriculum to provide immersive clinical training experiences and the opportunity for students to develop meaningful relationships with patients and faculty over time.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: The Burnett School of Medicine at TCU has a distributed model for its clinical training sites.  These sites are located throughout the DFW metro area.  Due to this model of training, students must have reliable transportation.  This can be accomplished through a personal vehicle, using a rideshare service (e.g., Lyft, Uber, etc.), or other options.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Casual clothing is acceptable in non-clinical environments. Clothing must fit properly, be clean, pressed, and modest. Torn, faded, frayed, ripped tight, sheer, or revealing clothing are not allowed.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Student Affairs is staffed during normal business hours. They provide an emergency number that staff monitor 24/7.  Peer tutoring is available. Course and clerkship directors offer office hours.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Students will be exposed early during the first year through the Introduction to Longitudinal Patient Care course.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: We employ an active learning and flipped classroom model. We utilize clinical application, team-based learning, and a combination of clinicians and basic scientists delivering each session.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: The school has a longitudinal integrated clerkship model comprised of eight core clerkships.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: While the Burnett School of Medicine at TCU doesn’t conduct formal lectures in the curriculum, there are mandatory sessions that students are required to attend weekly.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: Our curriculum integrates basic and clinical science through contextual experiences where student progress is measured through medical knowledge achievement and a developmental milestone model of competency performance. The structure consists of three sequential phases, with longitudinal courses and interdisciplinary curricular components woven throughout multiple phases. The pre-clinical curriculum, traditionally found over the first two years of medical school, spans 14 months. The Phase 1 timeline enables students to begin their Phase 2 clerkships sooner-giving them an opportunity to apply the knowledge they gain during Phase 1 in an experiential context across multiple specialties and health care arenas in Phase 2, and provides more time for individualized elective clinical experiences in Phase 3. Basic science content is revisited in Phases 2 and 3 with increased application.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Burnett School of Medicine at TCU has a robust four year scholarly pursuit and thesis course and also provides students additional resources and support to purse research endeavors.
medSchoolCurriculum.academicSystemText: The curriculum is comprised of three phases across four years.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: First-year students are required to complete 10 hours of community service.  During their third year, students will also participate in service through a required community impact project.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Students will be required to complete a scholarly research prospectus and culminating thesis throughout all four years of their medical education.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: We utilize a distributed model utilizing various hospitals within our campus vicinity and beyond.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation:
With a mission to transform health care by inspiring Empathetic Scholars™, a new allopathic school of medicine, the Burnett School of Medicine at TCU was created in Fort Worth, Texas.

This medical school was created in a transformative environment to address quality, cost and workforce challenges in a patient-centric model that utilizes advances in technology, enhances communication and focuses on patient safety.  With the goal of inspiring physicians who are Empathetic Scholars™, the medical school embraces proven learner-centered models, develops comprehensive strategies and advantages available and emerging technology.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
Our mission is to transform health care by inspiring Empathetic Scholars™.

Our Vision
To be a leader in medical education, delivery of care and scholarship. We do this by focusing intentionally on the constellation of:

Character – integrity, empathy, humanism, professionalism
Content – medical knowledge, technology, innovation, integration
Context – patient-centered models, cultural sensitivity, health care systems, finance, ambulatory settings, patient safety, chronic disease prevention and management
Creativity – innovation, inquisitive scholars
Collaboration – team-based care, patient and family partnerships, shared decision-making
Community – servant leadership, public education, partnership, leadership
Communication – exceptional communicators, active listeners

medSchoolApplication.cbcRequired: Yes, required at admission and at matriculation into the medical school.
medSchoolApplication.applicantResponseToOffer: Dependent upon time during the admission cycle.
medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: We require at least 1 letter of recommendation in order to move forward in the review process. However, the Office of Admissions highly recommends submitting three letters.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: An applicant must submit at least one letter of recommendation.    Recommenders are at the discretion of the applicant. A letter from a clinician is recommended but not required.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: Information about our interview day is given to applicants at the time they confirm their interview day.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: The Burnett School of Medicine at TCU participates in the virtual Multiple Mini-Interview (MMI) format through the KIRA platform.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: The Burnett School of Medicine at TCU participates in the virtual Multiple Mini-Interview (MMI) format through the KIRA platform.
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: Secondary applications are sent directly to TCU for review.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
Our admission process is virtual.   In keeping with this mission, our policies are designed to give all applicants the opportunity to showcase their journey to medicine.

Pre-Requisite Policy: Our pre-requisite policy allows applicants to take courses online, at four-year institutions and community colleges accredited in the United States and Canada.  Courses earned as Pass/Fail grades will be considered.  Rest assured, the impact of the COVID-19 situation will be taken into consideration when reviewing coursework and will not affect applicants negatively. 

MCAT Policy: Our MCAT policy indicates that we accept scores from the last three years - 2024, 2025, and 2026.

Candidates are invited to complete a secondary application based on an initial review of their primary application.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: Consideration is given to the highest MCAT score.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: Required coursework is accepted from accredited universities within the U.S. and Canada. This includes community colleges with this designation.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Students may upload in their portal letters of intent, updates, notices of significant updates, or achievements. There is no limit to the number of uploads a student may submit.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo:
The M.D. degree is a broad undifferentiated degree attesting to general knowledge in medicine and the basic skills required for entering residency training while meeting all requirements for medical licensure.  Essential abilities and characteristics required for completion of the M.D. degree consist of minimum physical and cognitive abilities, and mental and emotional health to assure that students, at admission, promotion, and graduation, are able to complete the entire course of study and participate fully in all aspects of medical training, with or without reasonable accommodation. Students who believe they may need to request reasonable accommodation(s) in order to meet the standards are encouraged to contact Texas Christian University (TCU) Student Access and Accommodation Office.

Please  review the link regarding our technical standards for more information.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: The Financial Education department within the Office of Admissions offers guidance and other important resources to students who seek financial aid to cover the expenses involved in attending the Burnett School of Medicine at TCU. Through individualized counseling, students will have access to information and resources that will help them plan a future of financial wellness beyond medical school.  Most students in the 2025-2026 academic year can expect a Burnett School of Medicine at TCU grant to cover fifteen percent of tuition.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
The Admissions Committee requires that in order to be eligible for matriculation, an applicant must have completed at least 90 semester hours (or equivalent quarter hours) in general education at a fully-accredited college or university in the United States or Canada by the time of matriculation. A bachelor’s degree is not required.

Regardless of field of study, the specific subjects listed below are required as prerequisites for admission. All prerequisite courses must be passed with a grade of B- or higher. The Admissions Committee will consider prerequisite courses earned through advanced placement (AP), college level examination program (CLEP) and courses graded “Pass/Fail”.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: We celebrate the differences in applicants’ personal stories and paths traveled to medicine, and commit to a comprehensive and holistic admissions approach that gives balanced and equal consideration of non-academic and academic factors, as well as the school-specific personal attributes required to be successful as a self-directed adult learner in the unique curriculum of training empathetic scholars. To this end, it is impossible to list the exact "recipe" for admission. However, applicants should be focused when preparing a competitive application in these four areas: leadership, service, physician/patient interactions, and research experience.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: The Burnett School of Medicine at TCU requires a minimum of 150 hours in Physician/Patient Interaction which could include but is not limited to EMT, medical scribe, Child Life Specialist, Nurse/Certified Nursing Assistant (CNA), shadowing, or medical assistant experiences.
